pr_title: agnhost: add functionality to inject out of order tcp packets
pr_body:
The test for regression issue 74839, was using its own image
named regression-issue-74839. It only works for IPv4

This adds the same functionaliy to the agnhost image, and
adds support for IPv6

This is the first step to fix
#93281

/kind failing-test
```release-note
NONE
```
pr_comments:
/assign @bowei 
There is a comment linking the code to you @bowei , I adapted it to use it with IPv6 too, can you PTAL?

So, this basically adds the functionality of the ``regression-issue-74839`` image into agnhost, right? Then, can we remove that image as well? I don't think we need the same functionality in 2 separate images.
yes, the other image can go away once the references to it have been removed

Gotcha. As for image promotion process, I've detailed the steps here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/images#making-changes-to-images (more specifically, in the 2nd half). But for a tl;dr version:

- this PR will have to merge first.
- wait for the postsubmit job to finish ( https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-testing-images#post-kubernetes-push-e2e-test-images )
- send update PR here with the newly built image's digest (you can get it by running: ``manifest-tool inspect --raw gcr.io/k8s-staging-e2e-test-images/${IMAGE_NAME}:${VERSION} | jq '.[0].Digest'``): https://github.com/kubernetes/k8s.io/blob/master/k8s.gcr.io/images/k8s-staging-e2e-test-images/images.yaml
- update your other PR you mentioned to also bump the agnhost version in ``test/utils/image/manifest.go``.
FWIW, the test passes on Windows with these agnhost changes on the updated test you've sent.
You might want to take a another look at what you commited. It seems like you've dropped some code after rebase.

> You might want to take a another look at what you commited. It seems like you've dropped some code after rebase.

hey, yep, that was on purpose, I just wanted to comment this with you @claudiubelu to ask for your opinion, let me explain:

I realised that for some each new networking scenario we need to create a custom golang pkg that need to go through all the promotion process, and this is slowing a lot the development of new test cases.

I've used before scapy, that is a very rich python framework to craft packages and do a lot of "nice" things with the network, and I was wondering if it would be it better to include it in the agnhost image so adding a new network feature is just creating a configmap with the python script, mount it as a volume and run it in the pod.

I'll add an example here so you can check how it will look like

/hold
